en: The steep pathways of the Banaue Rice Terraces act as inclined planes, reducing the effort needed to carry harvest baskets uphill.
Rubber-soled tsinelas provide high friction on dry school floors, preventing students from slipping during recess.
Earth's gravity pulls the water of Pagsanjan Falls downward, creating its famous cascading rapids.
Filipino fishermen navigate the West Philippine Sea using a magnetic compass that aligns with Earth's magnetic poles.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts the Earth's underground heat into usable electrical energy.
Alitaptap fireflies along Bohol's Loboc River produce visible light through a special chemical reaction in their abdomens.
Striking the brass gongs of a kulintang causes them to vibrate, producing sound waves that travel through the air.
An aluminum kawa pot quickly conducts heat from a charcoal fire to efficiently cook adobo.
A galloping horse pulling a kalesa through Vigan's cobblestone streets possesses kinetic energy due to its motion.
A single fixed pulley attached to a barangay water well changes the direction of force to lift heavy buckets.
Water friction against the wooden hull of a bangka slows its speed as it travels across Palawan's seas.
The electric motor inside a standard Philippine standing fan uses electromagnets to spin the blades and create wind.
